module purpose: neorv32_sdi holds a bus-written control register (an enable bit and five interrupt-source enables), pushes bus-written bytes into a TX FIFO sub-unit and pops received bytes from an RX FIFO sub-unit on bus reads, synchronizes the external serial clock, select and data inputs, and runs a serial engine that shifts a TX byte out on sdi_dat_o while shifting sdi_dat_i bits in and writing each completed byte into the RX FIFO; it raises irq_o when an enabled FIFO condition holds.

use-case flows.value: enable bit and five interrupt-source enable bits taken from bus write data at addr(2) = '0' and held in ctrl
transmit byte pushed from bus write data into the TX FIFO sub-unit at addr(2) = '1'
transfer start: in the enabled idle phase the TX FIFO byte (or zeros when it is empty) is loaded into the shift register and, on active select, a start pulse pops the TX FIFO
serial bit transfer: synchronized clock level changes sample sdi_dat_i, shift the register and count bits, while the register MSB drives sdi_dat_o
completed received byte written into the RX FIFO sub-unit
interrupt request from enabled FIFO conditions, and FIFO and select status bits on control reads
control register readback and received byte returned on bus reads, with an RX FIFO pop on a data read
ctrl, irq_o, synchronizer and serial-engine registers forced to zero while rstn_i = '0'; both FIFOs held clear and the engine held idle while ctrl.enable = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Serial interface enable setting -- whether the serial engine runs, the FIFOs keep their contents and interrupts can be raised
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 133) only when bus_req_i.stb = '1', rw = '1' and addr(2) = '0' (lines 130-132), reset to '0' (line 117). Module behavior depends on this held setting: `tx_fifo.clear <= not ctrl.enable;` (line 200) and `rx_fifo.clear <= not ctrl.enable;` (line 239) hold both FIFO sub-units clear while it is '0'; `serial.state(2) <= ctrl.enable;` (line 296, COPIES) makes the case arms "100", "110" and "111" (lines 299, 312, 322) reachable only while it is '1', the others arm returning the phase bits to "00" (line 338); and it gates irq_o (GATES at occurrence 7, line 249). Integrity is Established: a wrong value starts or stops the engine, clears queued bytes and masks interrupts against the written setting. Availability is also Established: while it is '0' no transfer starts, FIFO contents are discarded and no interrupt is raised. No line restricts reading it (line 143), so confidentiality is not established. ctrl.enable stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, line 133). bus_req_i carries complete requests (address, data, byte enables, strobe, read/write) and bus_rsp_o returns ack, err and data, so both are transport and are neither setting point nor exit; tx_fifo.clear and rx_fifo.clear only pass the inverted setting to the sub-units (lines 186, 221) and are carriers.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt-source enable settings -- which FIFO conditions may raise the interrupt request
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores five enable bits from bus write data (lines 135-139) under the predicates of lines 130-132, resets them to '0' (lines 118-122) and returns them on control reads (lines 147-151). The report flow depends on them: `irq_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_avail and rx_fifo.avail) or ...` (lines 249-254) admits each FIFO condition only when its enable is '1'. conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt request -- the registered decision that an enabled FIFO condition holds
conceptual assets.reasoning: The report flow registers `irq_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_avail and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_rx_half and rx_fifo.half) or (ctrl.irq_rx_full and (not rx_fifo.free)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)));` (lines 249-254) on each rising edge of clk_i (line 248), reset to '0' (line 247). The value leaves the entity on irq_o and its consumer is not supplied, so Integrity is Established: the consumer must receive exactly this expression. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: the request is recomputed at every clock edge while rstn_i is '1', and is forced low while ctrl.enable is '0'. irq_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM ctrl.irq_rx_avail at occurrence 3), which takes precedence over its storage role (CLOCKED_BY at the same occurrence). rx_fifo.avail, rx_fifo.half, rx_fifo.free and tx_fifo.half only receive sub-unit outputs and are read here as data (lines 250-254), so they are carriers; tx_fifo.avail is reported under its own concept.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmit data -- the byte loaded from the TX FIFO and shifted out serially
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow loads `serial.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata;` (line 305) in phase "100" when tx_fifo.avail is not '0' (zeros otherwise, line 303); the operate flow shifts it left on each detected serial clock change (line 327) and drives its MSB out with `sdi_dat_o <= serial.sreg(serial.sreg'left);` (line 345). The consumer of sdi_dat_o is outside this file, so Integrity is Established: sdi_dat_o must present the loaded byte bit by bit in the shift order of line 327. serial.sreg stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 5, line 305) and sdi_dat_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM serial.sreg at occurrence 2, line 345). The byte enters through bus_req_i.data, a transport field; tx_fifo.wdata (line 201) and tx_fifo.rdata (lines 195, 305) only pass it into and out of the tx_fifo_inst sub-unit, whose internals are not supplied, so they are carriers. No line restricts observation of sdi_dat_o, so confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Received data -- serial input bits assembled into a byte for the RX FIFO
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow samples the input with `sync.sdi_ff <= sync.sdi_ff(0) & sdi_dat_i;` (line 270), captures the synchronized bit with `serial.sdi_ff <= sync.sdi;` (line 314) in phase "110", and shifts it in with `serial.sreg <= serial.sreg(serial.sreg'left-1 downto 0) & serial.sdi_ff;` (line 327) on each detected clock change while select is active; when serial.cnt(3) = '1' (line 328) the byte is handed over by `rx_fifo.wdata <= serial.sreg;` (line 235) with `rx_fifo.we <= serial.done;` (line 236). The consumer is the rx_fifo_inst sub-unit, not supplied, so Integrity is Established: it must receive exactly the assembled byte. sdi_dat_i sets (SOURCES sync.sdi_ff at occurrence 2, line 270), sync.sdi_ff stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 270), serial.sdi_ff stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 314) and serial.sreg stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 6, line 327). sync.sdi only takes one bit of sync.sdi_ff (line 276) and rx_fifo.wdata only passes the byte to the sub-unit: both forward. The readback through bus_rsp_o.data (line 162) is transport and is not cited.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial transfer sequencing state -- engine phase and bit count within the current byte
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow is sequenced by `case serial.state is` (line 297): phase "100" clears the count and loads the register (lines 301-305) and moves to "110" on active select (line 309); "110" samples a bit and, on a clock change, increments `serial.cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(serial.cnt) + 1);` (line 318) and moves to "111" (line 319); "111" shifts (line 327) and, when serial.cnt(3) = '1', raises done and returns to "00" (lines 328-330), otherwise returns to "110" (line 332); deselect returns to "00" (lines 316, 325). The flow graph lists serial.cnt as self-updating, and serial.state selects its own next value (SELECTED_BY serial.state, lines 309-338). Integrity is Established: a corrupted phase or count shifts at the wrong time, ends a byte early or late, or hands a misaligned byte to the RX FIFO. serial.state stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 5, line 309) and serial.cnt stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 318); bit 2 of the phase copies ctrl.enable (line 296) and is covered under the enable concept.

conceptual assets.concept: Transfer start event -- the pulse that begins a transfer and pops the TX FIFO
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow raises `serial.start <= '1';` (line 308) in phase "100" when sync.csn = '0' (line 307), a one-cycle pulse cleared by the default `serial.start <= '0';` (line 292); `tx_fifo.re <= serial.start;` (line 205) delivers it to the re_i input of tx_fifo_inst (line 194). conceptual assets.concept: Byte-complete event -- the pulse that writes a received byte into the RX FIFO
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow raises `serial.done <= '1';` (line 329) in phase "111" on a clock change with select active when serial.cnt(3) = '1' (lines 324-328), a one-cycle pulse cleared by line 293; `rx_fifo.we <= serial.done;` (line 236) delivers it to the we_i input of rx_fifo_inst (line 226). That consumer is not supplied, so Integrity is Established: the RX FIFO must be written exactly once per completed byte, or received bytes are lost or duplicated. serial.done stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 5, line 329); rx_fifo.we only copies it into the sub-unit and is a carrier.

conceptual assets.concept: Select state -- the synchronized select level that starts and aborts transfers
conceptual assets.reasoning: The select input is sampled by `sync.csn_ff <= sync.csn_ff(0) & sdi_csn_i;` (line 269) and used as `sync.csn <= sync.csn_ff(1);` (line 275). The serial engine depends on it: sync.csn = '0' starts a transfer (lines 307-309), sync.csn = '1' returns phases "110" and "111" to idle (lines 315-316, 324-325), and it is reported as a status bit (line 160). Integrity is Established: a corrupted select level starts a transfer that pops the TX FIFO, or aborts a byte in progress. sdi_csn_i sets (SOURCES sync.csn_ff at occurrence 2, line 269) and sync.csn_ff stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 269). sync.csn only takes one bit of sync.csn_ff (line 275) and forwards it to the conditions; the status readback is through transport bus_rsp_o and is not cited.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial clock change event -- the detected level change of the sampled serial clock that paces sampling, shifting and counting
conceptual assets.reasoning: The serial clock input is sampled as data by `sync.sck_ff <= sync.sck_ff(1 downto 0) & sdi_clk_i;` (line 268), and its level changes are detected by `sync.sck <= sync.sck_ff(1) xor sync.sck_ff(2);` (line 274). conceptual assets.reasoning: `tx_fifo.we <= '1' when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '1') else '0';` (line 202) decides whether a bus access pushes bus_req_i.data(7 downto 0) (line 201) into the TX FIFO through we_i (line 191).
